summary.headline: KOEL Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 19% YoY to a record INR1,722 crores, but EBITDA fell 6% to INR191 crores as margin dropped to 11% on input inflation.
summary.overview: Standalone and consolidated revenue both hit record quarterly highs, with consolidated revenue at INR2,257 crores (up 17% YoY) and standalone at INR1,722 crores (up 19% YoY). Growth was broad-based across PowerGen, DABU, Fluid Dynamics and International, while Industrial grew only 2%. Margins compressed on crude, copper, aluminium and pig iron inflation: standalone EBITDA margin was 11% vs 14% a year ago, and net profit from continuing operations fell 14% YoY. Management said pricing actions are underway, that inflation is not fully passed through, and that Q2 could be the margin bottom if commodity costs plateau.

financial_highlights.change: vs 14% in Q2 FY26; down ~30 bps QoQ

financial_highlights.value: INR115 crores (transcript also reads INR1 15 crores)

financial_highlights.change: -5% YoY vs INR376 crores; margin vs 13.8%

financial_highlights.metric: H1 FY27 standalone net profit (continuing ops)

segments.name: PowerGen
segments.commentary: Revenue INR792 crores, up 17% YoY; management cites market share gains and 1010 kVA HHP node share above 30%. Volume and price split not disclosed.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Revenue INR381 crores, up 2% YoY; management attributed the weakness to execution challenges rather than demand. Pricing increases being taken with OEM partners.

segments.name: Distribution and Aftermarket (DABU)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR293 crores, up 29% YoY; whole goods and Nulife repowering/reconditioning are diversifying beyond spares.

segments.name: International (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR257 crores in the standalone presentation, up about 50% YoY; gross consolidated international revenue INR413 crores, up 59%, about 20% of sales mix. PowerGen is over 45% of international business.

segments.name: Fluid Dynamics (KOEL Fluid Dynamics)
segments.commentary: Operating revenue INR331 crores, up about 28% YoY; domestic sales up about 24%, exports up about 32%. Claims leadership in engine-driven industrial pumps.

segments.name: B2B (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,745 crores, up 20% YoY; segment PBIT INR148 crores.

segments.name: B2C (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR330 crores, up 28% YoY; segment PBIT INR23 crores, up 26% YoY.

segments.name: Arka Fincap (financial services)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR209 crores; segment PBT INR6.1 crores; H1 PAT INR11.5 crores; AUM INR7,781 crores; net NPA 0.5%; 146 branches. Management described FY27 as an investment year, with payback in 12-18 months.

guidance_outlook: Management targets INR2 billion (about $2 billion) ambition by FY30 and international at 30% of revenue within 2-3 years; Q4 is normally the strongest quarter.
Management expects operating leverage gains to begin in H2 FY27 or FY28, once incremental revenue absorbs capability costs already incurred.
Capex of around INR600-700 crores is planned for FY27 under the INR2,100 crore programme; first line due in FY28, and the INR1,400 crore programme is expected to start production around FY28-29.
Management said Q2 could be the bottoming quarter for margins if raw material inflation plateaus at current levels.
Arka expects investment-related drag to continue until 31 December 2026, with better-quality retail margins from Q1 FY28.
capex_capacity: Capex of INR2,100 crores announced and work started; first line expected to be operational in FY28.
INR1,400 crore capex programme announced last year; work started, with production hoped for FY28-29.
FY27 capex guidance of roughly INR600-700 crores, per analyst question; management said the capex programme is proceeding as planned.
HHP node strategy: 1010 kVA is the first HHP node in full mainstream execution; next nodes are 1250-1500 kVA, 2000 kVA, and above 2000 kVA.
Three new engine families in Tier 4 final certification in the Americas; one is linked to the DEUTZ 1.6 L platform programme.
demand_pricing: Management said demand remains robust across PowerGen, DABU and International, with PowerGen strength in MHP and HHP.
Pricing is being taken by product and customer; management said it will pass through inflation where possible and does not believe the pass-through is complete.
Data centre order: customer-side delay; the revised schedule is pending customer confirmation.
No delivery-lead-time elongation seen; customers are not open to longer delivery times.
Management does not look at peers' pricing when taking price increases; tender and contract timing lags pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Industrial grew only 2% YoY; is this a demand weakness?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Sahai said it was an execution issue, not demand or trajectory.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a PowerGen volume and price split?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Kejriwal said the company does not disclose PowerGen volume and price growth; Q2 PowerGen growth was 17%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise sharply, and when will operating leverage show?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Kejriwal cited the merit cycle starting in Q2, higher indirect and consumable costs from crude, and global marketing events. He said operating leverage should start in H2 FY27 or FY28 if execution holds.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone cash flow decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Kejriwal said cash from operations was positive in H1, and that strategic inventory build for project execution caused the temporary drop.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Arka profitability decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Samrat Gupta said FY27 is an investment year (distribution, technology, used-vehicle and small-ticket LAP), with 12-18 month paybacks and operations in seven states.

qa_highlights.question: How do you see margins recovering if commodities plateau?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Sahai said recovery depends on RM inflation plateauing. Management is confident of margin improvement through fixed cost control and internal cost-cutting, and Q2 could be the bottom if inflation holds constant.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation (crude, copper, aluminium, pig iron) continues to compress margins; the pass-through is incomplete.
Data centre order timing is delayed at the customer end; no updated schedule yet.
Industrial segment growth of 2% needs to recover after the execution issue.
Arka's profitability is down sharply (PBT down about 36% QoQ, 82% YoY) during the investment phase.
Standalone working capital build (inventory) is weighing on cash flow.
Other expenses are rising (merit increases, marketing events, indirect costs); operating leverage timing remains open.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line momentum and exports, but cautious and somewhat guarded on margins and near-term outlook. Management avoided quantifying pricing pass-through, HHP contribution, DEUTZ revenue, data centre timelines and the H2 outlook.
key_quotes: Our consolidated quarterly revenue crossed the INR2,000 crores threshold, reaching INR2,257 crores, our best quarter ever, representing a growth of 17% year-on-year and 14% quarter-on-quarter.

There are no one-timers in either of the businesses. There is a very core franchise that is being built, and we are only seeing the results of the work that we have been doing over the last couple of years.
If inflation held constant, then this could potentially be a bottoming out. We would see a directional improvement.

growth.why: Management reiterates a USD 2 billion ambition by FY30 and INR600-700 crore FY27 capex, with the first INR2,100 crore line due in FY28 and the INR1,400 crore programme around FY28-29; no explicit FY27 revenue growth number was given, and Q2 standalone revenue grew 19% on PowerGen, DABU and Fluid Dynamics strength, but operating leverage is only expected from H2 FY27 or FY28.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin fell to 11% from 14% YoY on crude, copper, aluminium and pig iron inflation; management says Q2 could be the bottom if RM plateaus and operating leverage starts H2 FY27 or FY28, but pass-through is incomplete.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: INR2,100 crore programme is under way with first line due FY28, and INR1,400 crore programme targets production around FY28-29; no new capacity in the FY27 window itself.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone revenue grew 19% YoY to INR1,722 crore on PowerGen (+17%, 1010 kVA node share above 30%), DABU (+29%) and Fluid Dynamics (+28%), though volume split is not disclosed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex of INR600-700 crore planned for FY27 under the INR2,100 crore programme, with work already started and management saying it is proceeding as planned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or margin guidance raise was given; management reiterated the USD 2 billion FY30 ambition and gave no explicit FY27 growth number.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margin fell about 300 bps YoY to 11% on RM inflation with pass-through not complete, and the data centre order is delayed at the customer end with no updated schedule.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Three new engine families are in Tier 4 final certification in the Americas, and HHP next nodes are 1250-1500 kVA, 2000 kVA and above; no firm launch dates were given.

rows.label: Price increases to pass through RM inflation
rows.why: Pricing is being taken by product and customer, management says pass-through is not complete, and tender and contract timing lags; standalone EBITDA margin was 11% vs 14% a year ago.

rows.label: Data centre order timing
rows.why: Customer-side delay, revised schedule pending customer confirmation, so timing of this order is uncertain.

rows.label: Inventory normalisation after project build
rows.why: Inventory is 63 days and the cash conversion cycle 31 days; the strategic build for project execution caused the H1 cash drop, and inventory fell 1 day QoQ.

tone.note: Management was confident on top-line momentum, exports, PowerGen share gains and the capex plan, but cautious on margins, pricing pass-through and the data centre timeline; analysts pressed on Industrial's 2% growth, cash flow, other expenses and Arka's profit decline.
